back2basics.text: Treasury Bills are short-term debt instruments issued by the government to meet temporary funding needs. They have maturities of less than one year and are issued at a discount to face value, with the difference representing interest. Auctions for these bills are conducted by the Reserve Bank of India to manage government borrowing and liquidity in the financial system.

2026-11-08-am-9b4d7d5f5f.deck: The Reserve Bank of India announced the auction of Government of India Treasury Bills with notified amounts of ₹8,000 crore for 91-day and 182-day bills, and ₹7,000 crore for 364-day bills. This auction is important for understanding government debt instruments, monetary policy operations, and financial market mechanisms.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the RBI auction of Treasury Bills:
1. The auction includes 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day Treasury Bills with a total notified amount of ₹23,000 crore.
2. Retail investors can participate only through competitive bidding with no allocation limits.
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because retail investors can participate on a non-competitive basis with allocation restricted to 5% of the notified amount.

body.label: Auction amounts
body.text: The auction includes ₹8,000 crore each for 91-day and 182-day Treasury Bills, and ₹7,000 crore for 364-day Treasury Bills, totaling ₹23,000 crore.

body.label: Auction and settlement dates
body.text: The auction is scheduled for November 11, 2026, with settlement on November 12, 2026.

body.label: Auction method
body.text: The auction uses a price-based multiple price method where bids are submitted electronically through RBI’s Core Banking Solution (E-Kuber).

sections.heading: What are the details of the RBI Treasury Bill auction?

body.label: Eligible participants
body.text: State Governments, Union Territories with legislatures, eligible Provident Funds, designated Foreign Central Banks, and RBI-specified persons or institutions can participate on a non-competitive basis.

body.label: Retail investor participation
body.text: Individuals can participate as retail investors on a non-competitive basis with allocation capped at 5% of the notified amount, and can also bid via the Retail Direct portal.

body.label: Bid submission timing
body.text: Competitive bids are accepted from 10:30 am to 11:30 am, and non-competitive bids from 10:30 am to 11:00 am on auction day.

sections.heading: Who can participate and how?
